useCase.name: Record servicing, repair and condition against an asset, with what it cost
useCase.featureRef: 18.9 Recording maintenance or a change of condition

intent.name: asset.maintenance.record
intent.summary: Record servicing, a repair, an inspection or a change of condition against an asset, with what it cost.

routesElsewhere.note: A maintenance record is never edited or deleted. A record entered wrongly is corrected by a further record, so the history stays a history (BR-7, E6, E7).

request.text: unserviceable hai to register se hata dein
request.gloss: it is unserviceable, take it off the register

routesElsewhere.note: An asset whose condition falls to unserviceable becomes a **candidate** for disposal and nothing disposes of it automatically. Disposal is its own decision with its own approval (BR-9, E8).

request.text: agli servicing ka waqt tay kar dein

routesElsewhere.note: Nothing schedules preventive maintenance. Every record is entered after the fact, and whether the school should be able to schedule one is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-1).

steps.note: One step, and it does two things: it writes the history and it **changes the asset's condition on the register**, so the register says what the asset is like now rather than what it was like when it was bought (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Where the cost cannot be posted to the ledger the record is not saved at all — a repair recorded with its cost lost is a maintenance total that understates itself from then on (E4).
plan.atomicity: One write with the ledger posting where there is a cost, through the ordinary voucher route for money leaving the school (BR-2). The condition on the register moves to what was recorded, and the total maintenance cost since purchase rises (BR-3, BR-6). Nothing here is ever edited or deleted (BR-7).

operations.name: asset.maintenance.record
operations.idempotencyKey: asset + date + cost, so a double press does not post the same repair to the ledger twice and double the maintenance total
operations.purpose: Record maintenance, servicing, inspection or a condition change against an asset.

parameters.name: asset_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No asset on the register matches, or it has been disposed of — maintenance cannot be recorded against a disposed asset (BR-8, E1).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the assets that match with their identifiers, locations and current conditions.

parameters.notes: The asset the work was done to.

parameters.name: maintenance_type
parameters.notes: What kind of work this was (BR-1). **Condition change only** is the case where no work was done at all — an asset found damaged, or degraded through use — and it carries no supplier and no cost (BR-4).

parameters.name: date
parameters.notes: When the work was done. Not in the future (E3).

parameters.name: supplier
parameters.notes: Who carried out the work. Required except for a condition change alone (BR-1, E2). Typed each time — no feature anywhere creates a supplier record, which the document names as a missing structure (OQ-4).

parameters.name: what_was_done
parameters.notes: 10 to 1000 characters, in the recorder's own words. This is what somebody deciding on a disposal years later actually reads (BR-5, BR-8).

parameters.name: cost
parameters.notes: What the work cost. Required except for a condition change alone, zero or more, and posted to the ledger where it is above zero (BR-2). Whether it affects the asset's book value or is expensed is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-2).

parameters.name: condition_after
parameters.notes: The asset's condition following the work. Required (BR-3, E5) — the register shows what the asset is like now, and this is the only thing that moves it.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What was done, what it cost, and what the asset is now.

fields.name: voucher
fields.description: The voucher the cost was posted through (BR-2).

fields.name: total_cost_since_purchase
fields.description: What the asset has cost the school in maintenance since it was bought (BR-6).

fields.name: purchase_value
fields.description: What it cost to buy. Set against the maintenance total, this is how an asset costing more to keep than to replace becomes visible — **nothing flags it** (BR-6, OQ-3).

fields.name: now_disposal_candidate
fields.description: True where the condition has fallen to unserviceable. A candidate only: nothing disposes of it, and disposal is its own decision with its own approval (BR-9, E8).

fields.name: editable
fields.description: False, always. A wrong record is corrected by a further record (BR-7, E6, E7).

errors.meaning: The asset has been disposed of.
No supplier was entered on a repair, servicing or inspection.
errors.note: A record with no date and no supplier cannot be checked against an invoice (BR-1).

errors.meaning: The date is in the future.

errors.notWritten: The record is not saved and nothing posts.
errors.note: The record and the posting hold together — a repair recorded with its cost lost understates the maintenance total from then on (BR-2, BR-6).
The register shows what the asset is like now, and this is the only thing that moves it (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Never guess the condition after. It is required, it is the only thing that moves the register's view of the asset, and it decides whether the asset becomes a disposal candidate (BR-3, BR-9, E5).

Say what the asset has now cost in total, against what it cost to buy. An asset costing more to keep than to replace is visible only when the two figures sit together, and **nothing flags it** (BR-6, OQ-3).

Say that unserviceable is a candidacy, not a disposal. Nothing retires an asset automatically — disposal is a separate decision with its own approval, and an unserviceable asset left alone stays on the register indefinitely (BR-9, E8).
Never offer to edit or delete a record. A wrong one is corrected by a further record, and both stay — that is what makes the maintenance history a history (BR-7, E6, E7).
Use a condition change only where no work was done. It carries no supplier and no cost, and recording a genuine repair that way loses the money from the asset's total (BR-4, BR-6).

reversal.statement: There is no reversal. A record entered wrongly is corrected by a **further** record with its own date and its own explanation, and both stay on the asset (BR-7, E6, E7). The cost already posted to the ledger is a matter for the finance module's own correction route.

request.text: projector ki marammat record kar dein — lamp module badla aur filter saaf kiya, Tech Care ne kiya, 9500 rupay
request.gloss: record the projector repair — lamp module replaced and filter cleaned, Tech Care did it, 9,500 rupees

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, projector currently Poor.

inputs.condition_after: asked — a repair usually improves it, but the answer is theirs

steps.note: The condition is asked rather than assumed (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Ask what condition it is in now — a repair usually improves it and only somebody who has seen it can say. After: report the cost posted and the total since purchase, PKR 23,200, against a purchase value of PKR 68,000. Add the fact nothing flags: this is the second lamp failure in eighteen months.

request.text: ye laptop gir kar toot gaya hai, ab chalta nahi
request.gloss: this laptop was dropped and is broken, it does not work now

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, no repair attempted.

steps.note: A condition change with no supplier and no cost (PR-5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Recorded as a condition change — no work was done, so there is no supplier and no cost. The laptop is now a **candidate** for disposal and nothing more: nothing retires it, and if nobody raises a disposal it stays on the register as unserviceable indefinitely.

request.text: pichla record ghalat tha, us mein 9500 ki jagah 5900 tha
request.gloss: the last record was wrong, it was 5,900 not 9,500

inputs.what_was_done: a correction to the earlier record, in their words

steps.note: A further record, because nothing is editable (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The earlier record cannot be edited or deleted. The correction goes on as a further record naming what it corrects, and both stay — which is what keeps the maintenance history a history rather than a current opinion. Note that the ledger already carries the original posting, and correcting that is the finance module's own route.

intent.name: asset.maintenance.read
intent.summary: See what an asset has cost to keep, what has been done to it, and what state it is in now.
routesHere: what has this projector cost us since we bought it?

routesHere.text: is projector par ab tak kitna kharch ho chuka hai?
routesHere.gloss: how much has been spent on this projector so far?

routesHere.text: is asset ki marammat ka record dikhayein

routesHere: show me everything repaired this year and what it cost

routesElsewhere.note: Retiring an asset is a decision with its own approval, and the approver sees this history before making it (BR-5, BR-8).
Where an asset has been is the assignment history. What has been done to it is here.

request.text: depreciation ke baad ki qeemat kya hai?
request.gloss: what is its value after depreciation?

routesElsewhere.note: Nothing calculates depreciation and no asset carries a remaining book value. Whether maintenance cost affects book value is unanswered, and nothing computes a book value at all (OQ-2).

steps.note: One read. Nothing changes on the asset or on the register.

plan.atomicity: A read. The record is append only — nothing in it is ever edited or deleted (BR-7).

operations.name: asset.maintenance.read
operations.purpose: Return maintenance records, costs and conditions.

parameters.name: asset_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No asset matches, registered or disposed of.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the assets that match with their identifiers and conditions.

parameters.notes: Where the question is about one asset, including one already disposed of — its history stays readable (BR-5, UC-18-07 BR-8).

parameters.name: condition
parameters.notes: Where the question is about what state things are in — unserviceable assets are the disposal candidates (BR-9).

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.notes: The start of the period asked about.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What has been spent and what state things are in.

fields.name: records
fields.description: Date, type, supplier, what was done, cost, condition before and condition after.

fields.name: total_cost_since_purchase
fields.description: What the asset has cost in maintenance since it was bought (BR-6).

fields.name: purchase_value
fields.description: What it cost to buy, from the voucher on the register (UC-18-07 BR-3).

fields.name: costs_more_than_it_cost
fields.description: Assets whose maintenance total now exceeds their purchase value. **Nothing flags this** — the figures are shown and no rule acts on them (BR-6, OQ-3).

fields.name: unserviceable
fields.description: Assets that are disposal candidates. Nothing disposes of them and an unserviceable asset nobody raises a disposal for stays on the register indefinitely (BR-9, E8).

fields.name: repeat_repairs
fields.description: Assets repaired more than once for the same kind of fault. This is what somebody deciding on a disposal is really asking about (BR-5, BR-8).

fields.name: condition_changes_without_work
fields.description: Records where the condition moved and no work was done — an asset found damaged or degraded through use (BR-4).

fields.name: no_maintenance_ever
fields.description: Assets with no record at all. Either nothing has ever gone wrong, or nothing has ever been recorded, and the two look identical (BR-1).

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the maintenance history.
errors.note: The use case writes no exception for it.

planningRules.rule: Give the maintenance total against the purchase value, always together. An asset costing more to keep than to replace is only visible as a comparison, and nothing in the system makes it (BR-6, OQ-3).
Name the unserviceable assets nobody has raised a disposal for. They are candidates and nothing acts on the candidacy, so they sit on the register unretired and still counted in its total (BR-9, E8).
Name the repeat repairs. Two lamp failures in eighteen months is the fact a disposal decision turns on, and it is buried in a list of dated records (BR-5, BR-8).
Say when an asset has no maintenance record at all, and that it means nothing on its own. Never repaired and never recorded look identical here (BR-1).
Never present a value after depreciation. Nothing calculates one anywhere in the system (OQ-2).

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing. The record it reads can never be edited or deleted (BR-7).

request.text: is projector par ab tak kitna kharch ho chuka hai?
request.gloss: how much has been spent on this projector so far?

resolvedPlans.outcome: PKR 23,200 in maintenance against PKR 68,000 to buy — give both, because one without the other says nothing. Then the fact behind the number: the lamp module has been replaced twice in eighteen months, which is what a disposal decision actually turns on and is not visible in a total.

List them with how long each has been unserviceable. Say plainly that nothing retires them: they are candidates and no rule acts on the candidacy, so they stay on the register, still counted in its total value, until somebody raises a disposal for each one.
